security_audit.summary: Actual bash examples in PROCESS.md and SKILL.md instruct users to run npx claude-flow@alpha, so those command blocks remain confirmed medium risks. Many static hits were only markdown fences, headings, or diagrams and were marked false positive. No prompt injection, credential access, or data exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: External commands use the mutable npx claude-flow@alpha package tag.
remediation.suggestion: Pin a reviewed package version and tell users to inspect each command before execution.

remediation.issue: Command examples create local output files and may start monitoring processes.
remediation.suggestion: Add safety notes about workspace location, generated files, and stopping long-running monitors.

remediation.issue: The skill assumes Claude Flow is installed and trusted.
remediation.suggestion: Document installation trust requirements and avoid auto-running commands from the skill text.

content.user_title: Chain Agent Pipelines With Streamed Outputs
content.value_statement: Agent workflows often lose context between stages. This skill shows how to pass outputs through memory or streams with validation steps.
actual_capabilities: Outlines sequential, parallel, and hybrid agent pipeline patterns.
Shows how to connect agent stages through memory or streams.
Provides Claude Flow command examples for design, execution, monitoring, and validation.
Defines success criteria for latency, throughput, error rate, and data integrity.
Lists common pipeline issues and practical solutions.
limitations: Relies on Claude Flow commands that must be installed and trusted by the user.
Does not provide runnable application code beyond command examples and workflow steps.
Does not verify package integrity, command output, or environment safety.
Assumes users understand agent coordination and pipeline concepts.

use_cases.title: Plan Release Automation
use_cases.description: Design a staged release workflow where research, coding, testing, and review agents pass validated outputs forward.

use_cases.title: Connect AI Research Flows
use_cases.description: Route findings from one agent into analysis and synthesis agents without losing intermediate state.

use_cases.title: Monitor Pipeline Quality
use_cases.description: Track latency, throughput, backpressure, and validation results across chained agent stages.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Basic Pipeline
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a small sequential workflow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a three-stage research, code, and test pipeline. Show each stage, input, output, and validation point.

prompt_templates.title: Add Streaming Between Stages
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate conversion from memory passing to streamed data flow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert my existing agent pipeline into a stream-based flow. Identify channels, buffers, monitoring points, and error handling.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Pipeline Strategies
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning for mixed sequential and parallel work.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this task list and propose sequential, parallel, and hybrid agent pipeline options. Explain tradeoffs and selection criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Operate a Production Pipeline
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced operational design with monitoring and recovery.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a monitored agent pipeline for a release workflow. Include state management, backpressure handling, validation, and recovery steps.

output_examples.input: A user needs agents to research issues, implement fixes, test results, and review quality.
output: A sequential four-stage pipeline is recommended.
Each stage receives the prior validated output as input.
Testing and review stages include pass criteria before completion.

output_examples.input: A user wants faster processing for independent analysis tasks.
output: A hybrid pipeline splits independent analysis into parallel branches.
A merge stage combines branch outputs after validation.
Monitoring tracks throughput and backpressure across channels.

output_examples.input: A user asks how to prevent data loss between streamed agent stages.
output: The workflow adds acknowledgments, validation checkpoints, and retry handling.
Intermediate state is stored before each downstream handoff.

best_practices: Review each external command before execution and pin trusted package versions.
Define stage inputs, outputs, validation points, and failure handling before running agents.
Monitor throughput, latency, backpressure, and data integrity during long workflows.
anti_patterns: Running npx commands from examples without confirming package source and version.
Passing unvalidated outputs directly into later agents.
Adding parallelism before dependencies and merge rules are clear.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps design chained agent pipelines where each stage passes validated output to the next stage.

faq.question: Can it support parallel pipelines?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes sequential, parallel, and hybrid patterns for agent coordination.

faq.question: Does it run commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides command examples that users must review and run themselves.

faq.question: Which tools does the skill reference?
faq.answer: The instructions reference Claude Flow commands and are listed for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code users.

faq.question: What should I check before using it?
faq.answer: Confirm the Claude Flow package source, version, permissions, and output paths before running any command.

faq.question: Does it handle production monitoring?
faq.answer: It outlines monitoring metrics, but users must configure real alerts and operational controls separately.
